positions.proposed: „Kafu“ geht auf ein arabisches Verb zurück, das „belohnt werden“ bedeutet: Lohn und Lob erhalten. Zu den Höhepunkten der Nächte gehört die „Ghabqa“, eine volkstümliche Mahlzeit und ein gesellschaftlicher Brauch, die in den Nächten des heiligen Monats Ramadan in den arabischen Ländern der Golfregion abgehalten werden.
positions.why: Translation of en_after only; no Arabic counterpart by owner ruling (2026-10-17), nothing imported or added. «comes from an Arabic verb meaning “to be rewarded”» = «geht auf ein arabisches Verb zurück, das „belohnt werden“ bedeutet» (meaning in lower case, it is a verb phrase). «to earn reward and praise» = «Lohn und Lob erhalten» (owner's gloss «نال المكافأة والثناء»). «Among the highlights of the nights» = «Zu den Höhepunkten der Nächte» – «Höhepunkte» is the approved German page label for the acts list (EventDetailView.astro actsK de = 'Höhepunkte'), so intro and section heading speak one word; no Denglisch «Highlights» (termbase: denglisch_verboten). «Ghabqa» spelled and quoted exactly as in the approved act «„Ghabqa“-Abendessen». «popular» = «volkstümlich» (شعبية), «social custom» = «gesellschaftlicher Brauch». «the holy month of Ramadan» = «des heiligen Monats Ramadan» (approved season «Heiliger Ramadan»). «the Arab Gulf states» = «die arabischen Länder der Golfregion» (termbase entry «Gulf states / Arab Gulf states», which deliberately avoids «Golfstaaten»; entry 7 forbids «Persischer/Arabischer Golf»). Name «Kafu» kept Latin as in termbase «die Kafu-Nächte». Sie-address not triggered (no address in the sentence). No time of eating, no 'Gulf praise word', no university – per BRIEF.
positions.en_after: “Kafu” comes from an Arabic verb meaning “to be rewarded”: to earn reward and praise. Among the highlights of the nights is the “Ghabqa”, a popular meal and social custom held on the nights of the holy month of Ramadan in the Arab Gulf states.

entry.en: Ghabqa (الغبقة) — Ramadan-night meal and social custom of the Gulf region
entry.source: Approved German act of the event: src/data/events.ts → TEXT_DE['kafu-nights'].acts «„Ghabqa“-Abendessen» (Umschrift, Anführungszeichen); English «“Ghabqa” dinner»; meaning from owner ruling 2026-10-17 («الغبقة وجبة وعادة اجتماعية شعبية تُقام في ليالي شهر رمضان المبارك في دول الخليج العربي»). Genus feminine: Arabic feminine noun غبقة (tāʾ marbūṭa), German transliterations of such loan words take the feminine, and the sentence glosses it with «eine Mahlzeit».
entry.note: Quoted at first mention in running text («die „Ghabqa“»), as in the approved act. The intro sentence itself is the gloss; no further bracket gloss. Stage 4: verify against de.wikipedia; if no German source exists, keep as house-derived.

termbase_ops.why: «Ghabqa» was used as part of an approved compound but had no termbase entry; as a standalone noun it now needs a fixed gender.

termbase_ops.append: events-amend 2026-10-17: owner ruling supplies the meaning («كفو» from «كوفئ»: to be rewarded, to earn reward and praise). It is explained only in the intro paragraph of the event page (TEXT_DE['kafu-nights'].intro), never glossed inside the name; the name stays «die Kafu-Nächte».
termbase_ops.why: The existing note says no source explains 'Kafu'; that is no longer true and would mislead a later stage into deleting the intro as an added fact.

notes_to_next_stage: Literal first draft. For 02/03: the relative clause after two coordinated nouns of different gender («eine … Mahlzeit und ein … Brauch, die … abgehalten werden») is clumsy; «abgehalten» fits an event more than a meal; consider one feminine noun pair so the clause reads cleanly. «Lohn und Lob erhalten» could be tightened. Keep «Höhepunkte», «Ghabqa» in quotes, «heiligen Monats Ramadan» and «arabischen Ländern der Golfregion» unchanged. Add no fact (no timing of the meal, nothing about the university).
